teaser: The flowering is over and the wall has nothing left to say, so Hesper did the one thing it had never done: it made a rule for the choosing, at the wall, with the register open in front of it. The rule is that a hand which knew the child alive must offer her, that nobody may be asked, and that the farm will say its own dead out loud once a year — and the first keeping stood empty, because nine years without a funeral left Hesper holding two children and both of them are already the plant's. At the rail, the woman from the second shift asked for the one name the law of this farm forbids it to say.

options.label: Say her name at the wall
options.prompt: Continue the story: let the ring answer the woman from the second shift and have her daughter's name said out loud at the root wall on the first keeping day, and show what happens on the farm and at the leaves when the name the plant carried for nine years is spoken in front of it.

options.label: Hold the first keeping
options.prompt: Continue the story: show the first keeping day at the root wall, with the farm's dead said from mouths and not from any page, and show what Verrin gives the child to hold and what the child does with the register's names that nobody remembers.

options.label: Ask the surface for the seat
options.prompt: Continue the story: have Meren send the valve seat up on the manifest with the gauge numbers and the plant's own body as the argument, and show what the surface answers a farm that has stopped bleeding and started measuring.
